standard_prerequisites.name: Descent data as cartesian simplicial schemes
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 6941-6943: Y -> (X/S)_bullet is the cartesian morphism of simplicial schemes corresponding to (V, phi), with Y_0 = V.

standard_prerequisites.name: Equivalence classes of closed points with finite classes
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 6946-6951: v_i the unique closed point of Spec(A_i); i ~ j iff v_i in T_{v_j}; by the two cited lemmas this is an equivalence relation with finite equivalence classes.

standard_prerequisites.name: Affineness of finite unions of Artinian spectra
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 6960-6963: V_{i-bar} finite union of spectra of Artinian local rings, so V_{i-bar} -> X is affine.

standard_prerequisites.name: Effectiveness of affine descent data along fpqc coverings
standard_prerequisites.use: Proof lines 6964-6971: {X -> S} is an fpqc covering, so each affine descent datum (V_{i-bar}, phi_{i-bar}) is effective.

core_obligations: Reduction to the cartesian simplicial scheme (proof lines 6941-6945): let Y -> (X/S)_bullet correspond to (V, phi), so Y_0 = V; write V = disjoint union of Spec(A_i) with A_i local Artinian and let v_i be the unique closed point.

Equivalence classes and the splitting (lines 6946-6959): set i ~ j iff v_i in T_{v_j}; an equivalence relation with finite classes by the cited lemmas; writing V as the disjoint union of V_{i-bar} over I/~, the isomorphism phi maps the open-and-closed subspaces V_{i-bar} x_S X into X x_S V_{i-bar}, so one gets descent data (V_{i-bar}, phi_{i-bar}) and (V, phi) is their coproduct in the category of descent data.

Effectiveness (lines 6960-6971): each V_{i-bar} is a finite union of spectra of Artinian local rings, hence V_{i-bar} -> X is affine; since {X -> S} is an fpqc covering, each (V_{i-bar}, phi_{i-bar}) is effective by the Descent affine lemma, and therefore so is their coproduct (V, phi).
proof_roadmap: Translate the descent datum into the cartesian simplicial scheme Y -> (X/S)_bullet.
Partition V by the equivalence relation on closed points and observe phi preserves the open-and-closed pieces.
Conclude effectiveness of each affine piece by the fpqc affine descent lemma, hence of the coproduct.
difficulty_reason: Descent lemma (statement 6933-6939, proof 6941-6971): reduces effectiveness for a disjoint union of Artinian spectra to finitely many affine pieces - the partition via the equivalence relation on closed points has finite classes (cited lemmas), phi preserves the open-and-closed decomposition so the datum splits as a coproduct, and each piece is affine with effective descent data by the fpqc affine lemma; no verification is omitted. H2: descent bookkeeping reducing to the affine case.
